meta.title: Netcap file evidence: reconstruct, preserve, classify

nodes.label: Audit output ready
nodes.sublabel: Only if all required work passes

cards.title: Bytes and observations have different identities
items: Recovered bytes are published atomically without overwriting another file. Configured content deduplication can reuse storage; transfer observations remain independent (save_file_enhanced.go:356-476).
Stored content does not require a File audit row: WriteFile returns when the File decoder has no writer. The writer-selected arrow is a separate output condition (file.go:39-54).

A File record includes content hashes, transfer endpoints and completeness. Hash remains the legacy MD5 field; use Hashes.SHA256 for evidence (save_file_enhanced.go:507-535; docs/file-extraction.md:17).
Extraction is separate from payload retention and keeping a source PCAP (docs/file-extraction.md:3).

cards.title: Optional analyzers are qualified work
items: Capture startup freezes analyzer configuration, rules and tool digests. Requested YARA needs a supporting build and enabled rules; requested Magika needs its executable (analysis_runtime.go:123-176).
Analysis uses a bounded queue and a content-hash cache. A caller waits for its admitted result; repeated transfers can share analysis (analysis_runtime.go:354-416).
artifact-analysis.json records job states and coverage; capture finalization drains accepted jobs before sealing output (analysis_runtime.go:483-522).

cards.title: A saved file may be incomplete
items: Encryption, stream gaps, declared lengths and decoder support constrain extraction. Inspect IsComplete and CompletenessReason (docs/file-extraction.md:3,30,95-97).
If requested analysis fails, preserved bytes remain but coverage is partial and output is not marked ready (internal/collector/cleanup.go:113-126).
The Web UI and MCP can inspect extraction and analyzer results. Manual post-capture YARA scans are a separate workflow (docs/file-extraction.md:65,69-93).
